claims: The International Space Station (ISS) is a habitable artificial satellite in low Earth orbit.
The International Space Station (ISS) serves as a microgravity research laboratory for NASA (USA), Roscosmos (Russia), ESA (Europe), JAXA (Japan), and CSA (Canada).
The International Space Station (ISS) operates at ~408 km altitude.
The International Space Station (ISS) has been continuously inhabited since 2000.
As of early April 2026, the International Space Station (ISS) is transitioning crew, including Expedition 74 members.
Expedition 74 members recently engaged in joint operations with Artemis II.
The International Space Station (ISS) orbits roughly every 90 minutes.
The International Space Station (ISS) conducts scientific research in biology, human physiology, and physics.
The International Space Station (ISS) tests technologies for space exploration.
The total costs of the International Space Station (ISS) are estimated to exceed $100 billion over its lifespan.
The costs of the International Space Station (ISS) are shared by international partners.
The International Space Station (ISS) is a 420-tonne structure.
The International Space Station (ISS) has over 916 cubic meters of pressurized space.
The International Space Station (ISS) is expected to continue operations until 2030.
The International Space Station (ISS) is planned to be deorbited after 2030.
